newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish BGZ bank could increase own funds.
newsitem.headline: Polish BGZ bank could increase own funds.

text.p: Polish state-owned Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA (BGZ) is likely to increase its own funds by 700 million zlotys from 1.6 billion by the end of the year, the chairman of the bank's supervisory board said.

Antoni Magdon said that if the finance minister approved the bank's report on carrying out its debt restructuring programme it could award the bank 600 million zlotys worth of bonds for its own funds and later an additional 100 million.
"BGZ had to report on the restructuring programme to receive the restructuring bonds. There is still a question whether it was carried out properly," Magdon told Reuters.
He added that BGZ could receive the bonds at the end of September.
BGZ Chief Accountant Jerzy Busz said the bank had fulfilled all the requirements to receive the bonds and was expecting ministry acceptance of the debt restructuring programme.
BGZ had a net profit of 187 million zlotys last year after losses of 3.1 billion zlotys over recent years.
It expects to have a pre-tax profit of 411 million zlotys this year.
